answerText: A brand domain (often referred to as the second-level domain or SLD) is the core, unique identifier of a website located between the subdomain and the top-level domain (TLD). For example, in the URL [www.website.com](https://www.website.com) : Subdomain: www Brand Domain: website Top-Level Domain (TLD): com Key Concepts & Uses Brand Consistency & Trust: Using your brand domain for tracking links, email servers, and web hosting ensures customers recognize your business immediately, reducing friction and avoiding spam filters [1.1.1, 1.1.7]. Attribution & Deep Linking: Platforms like AppsFlyer allow businesses to use custom branded domains (e.g., click.yourbrand.com ) instead of generic short links to drive higher click-through rates [1.1.1]. Content Management: Marketing and CMS platforms (such as HubSpot) utilize brand domains to govern how websites, blogs, and landing pages are hosted across primary and secondary subdomains [1.1.3, 1.1.9]. Relevant Resources & Documentation For details on mapping and customizing domains for tracking and campaigns, check out the AppsFlyer Branded Domains Guide [1.1.1]. To learn how to manage, connect, or replace brand domains across multi-channel web hosting, visit the HubSpot Domains and URLs Knowledge Base [1.1.3]. If you are looking for help with a specific platform setup or DNS configuration regarding your brand domain, please let me know what tools you are using!
